timeline.event: Synthetic alert and user reports indicate repeated request failures.
Incident coordinator assigns service and dependency investigation roles.
A fictional dependency saturation condition is identified.
Traffic is shifted to the documented fallback path.
User-visible checks show the fictional service behavior restored.

postmortem.narrative: A detailed fictional chronology explains detection, coordination, dependency saturation, fallback use, restoration, and residual risk.
contributing_conditions: Fallback capacity assumption had not been revalidated after a fictional demand-model change.
Dependency saturation was visible in a specialist view but not in the primary service dashboard.
lessons: A detailed narrative does not itself prove that a corrective action was completed or effective.
Follow-through should retain completion and later effectiveness evidence separately.

corrective_actions.description: Revalidate fallback-capacity assumptions before the next fictional peak period.
Add dependency saturation context to the service investigation guide.
Create a new always-on duplicate dependency monitor.

changed_approach.rationale: The fictional duplicate monitor would add maintenance without improving the primary diagnostic gap.
changed_approach.replacement_action: Add dependency saturation to the existing user-journey diagnostic view and exercise it during the next tabletop.

timeline.event: Synthetic user-journey check detects a sign-in failure.
Responder identifies a stale fictional configuration value.

postmortem.narrative: A concise fictional postmortem links the stale configuration to a missing pre-release comparison step.
contributing_conditions: Configuration comparison was manual and omitted during an urgent maintenance path.
lessons: The useful learning claim depends on later evidence that the new comparison step is both adopted and catches the relevant drift.

corrective_actions.description: Add a configuration-difference review to the fictional urgent-maintenance checklist.
